cases.question: A visual dairy delivery has bindings to three nonexistent materials. The producer says the overview image looks plausible. What needs review before accepting the saved asset?

The distribution-centre brief did not require authored normals. A separately chosen general rule rejected 121,602 meshes for missing them. The brief-specific rows passed. Is producer repair the only decision needed?

A parcel arrives on time, but separate review finds the indicator shows a different route between events. The intended demonstration must communicate the route accurately. Is passing endpoint timing enough?

The brief permits any legible neutral surface color for a visual layout. Delivered gray differs from the producer’s initial blue sketch. Binding and readability evidence is present; no exact color is required.
The requested deliverable predicts whether a part will slip. The producer selected friction from how shiny the render looks. No measured contact data is supplied.

The brief explicitly requests a low-friction slipping variant for teaching. The observed displacement matches that approved variant, while an advisory comparison differs from a nominal high-friction reference.
A required backside safety label must be legible. Only a front render is supplied. The producer says it used the same font on both sides.
The owner permits triangles for a static visualization. The delivered mesh is triangulated, the selected geometry checks pass, and no editability or quad-only policy applies.

The brief requests a physically credible fixed-length transfer arm. The producer scales the arm during transfer to reach each position. A few endpoint views appear plausible; no intermediate length evidence is supplied.

The owner needs interactive navigation. The producer reports around 4.5 draw callbacks per second while orbiting a large scene in Blender, but has not measured displayed FPS with a defined camera path. Structural rules pass.
